{
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    # The object with a patterned interior acts as a mask for the next outlined frame;
    # copy its interior pattern into that frame, preserving the frame's border.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    # identify rectangular colored frames and filled-pattern sources by connected colors
    from collections import deque
    seen=set(); objs=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color=grid[r][c]
            if color==0 or (r,c) in seen: continue
            q=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
            while q:
                y,x=q.pop(); cells.append((y,x))
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=ny<h and 0<=nx<w and (ny,nx) not in seen and grid[ny][nx]==color:
                        seen.add((ny,nx)); q.append((ny,nx))
            minr=min(y for y,x in cells); maxr=max(y for y,x in cells); minc=min(x for y,x in cells); maxc=max(x for y,x in cells)
            objs.append((color,cells,minr,maxr,minc,maxc))
    # Target frames have border-only (hollow) content; source is an irregular colored pattern.
    # Pattern cells are mapped by relative row/column scaling to each available hollow frame,
    # taking source object's bbox interior as the bitmap.
    patterns=[]; frames=[]
    for color,cells,r0,r1,c0,c1 in objs:
        cellset=set(cells); bh=r1-r0+1; bw=c1-c0+1
        border={(r,c) for r,c in cells if r in (r0,r1) or c in (c0,c1)}
        if len(border)==len(cells):
            frames.append((color,r0,r1,c0,c1))
        else:
            patterns.append((color,r0,r1,c0,c1,cellset))
    # infer source patterns displayed in frame regions: demo's 8-color pattern maps into 6 frame,
    # while 5-frame maps into 4-frame. In general each irregular pattern maps to nearest
    # outlined frame by center distance, with source color pattern preserved as target frame color.
    for pcol,pr0,pr1,pc0,pc1,pcs in patterns:
        choices=[]
        for fcol,fr0,fr1,fc0,fc1 in frames:
            if (fr0,fr1,fc0,fc1)==(pr0,pr1,pc0,pc1): continue
            dist=abs((pr0+pr1-fr0-fr1))+abs((pc0+pc1-fc0-fc1))
            choices.append((dist,fcol,fr0,fr1,fc0,fc1))
        if not choices: continue
        _,fcol,fr0,fr1,fc0,fc1=min(choices)
        # Map source bbox interior proportionally to target interior. For consistent sizes
        # use nearest-neighbor indexing over the interior rectangles.
        sh,sw=pr1-pr0-1,pc1-pc0-1; th,tw=fr1-fr0-1,fc1-fc0-1
        if sh<=0 or sw<=0 or th<=0 or tw<=0: continue
        for i in range(th):
            for j in range(tw):
                sy=pr0+1+min(sh-1,round(i*(sh-1)/max(1,th-1)))
                sx=pc0+1+min(sw-1,round(j*(sw-1)/max(1,tw-1)))
                if (sy,sx) in pcs: out[fr0+1+i][fc0+1+j]=fcol
                else: out[fr0+1+i][fc0+1+j]=0
    return out

{
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]); out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # Detect solid rectangular frames (one-cell perimeter) by their complete boundary.
    frames=[]
    for color in range(1,10):
        pts=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]==color]
        if not pts: continue
        r0=min(r for r,c in pts); r1=max(r for r,c in pts); c0=min(c for r,c in pts); c1=max(c for r,c in pts)
        edge=[(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if r in (r0,r1) or c in (c0,c1)]
        if len(edge)>=8 and all(grid[r][c]==color for r,c in edge):
            frames.append((color,r0,r1,c0,c1))
    # Motif source is a frame with marked cells in its aperture; duplicate its
    # binary pattern into any same-sized frame. Other outlined rectangles stay intact.
    stencils=[]
    for frame in frames:
        color,r0,r1,c0,c1=frame
        bitmap=[[grid[r][c]==color for c in range(c0+1,c1)] for r in range(r0+1,r1)]
        if any(any(row) for row in bitmap): stencils.append((frame,bitmap))
    if not stencils: return out
    # Choose stencil whose interior has the most marked cells; it's the intentionally patterned one.
    src,bitmap=max(stencils,key=lambda item:sum(sum(row) for row in item[1]))
    scol,sr0,sr1,sc0,sc1=src; sh,sw=len(bitmap),len(bitmap[0]) if bitmap else 0
    for color,r0,r1,c0,c1 in frames:
        if (color,r0,r1,c0,c1)==src: continue
        if r1-r0-1!=sh or c1-c0-1!=sw: continue
        for i in range(sh):
            for j in range(sw): out[r0+1+i][c0+1+j]=color if bitmap[i][j] else 0
    return out

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]);out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # The rule applies to each isolated rectangular border: replace the interior of
    # the frame with the pattern shown in a same-size frame, in that frame's color.
    frames=[]
    for color in range(1,10):
        pts=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]==color]
        if not pts:continue
        r0=min(r for r,c in pts);r1=max(r for r,c in pts);c0=min(c for r,c in pts);c1=max(c for r,c in pts)
        border={(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if r in (r0,r1) or c in (c0,c1)}
        if len(border)>=8 and all(grid[r][c]==color for r,c in border):frames.append((color,r0,r1,c0,c1))
    # For each matching-size family, the interior from the nonempty frame is the motif.
    families={}
    for f in frames:
        color,r0,r1,c0,c1=f; ih,iw=r1-r0-1,c1-c0-1
        if ih<=0 or iw<=0:continue
        bitmap=[[grid[r][c]==color for c in range(c0+1,c1)] for r in range(r0+1,r1)]
        count=sum(sum(row) for row in bitmap)
        families.setdefault((ih,iw),[]).append((count,f,bitmap))
    for family in families.values():
        nonblank=[x for x in family if x[0]>0]
        if not nonblank:continue
        # The sparsest motif-bearing frame is the source; apply to all other panels.
        _,source,bits=min(nonblank,key=lambda x:x[0])

            for i in range(len(bits)):
                for j in range(len(bits[0])):out[r0+1+i][c0+1+j]=color if bits[i][j] else 0
    return out

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    for r in range(h):

            stack = [(r, c)]

            cells = set()
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop()
                cells.add((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
                    ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
                    if (0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and (ny, nx) not in seen
                            and grid[ny][nx] == color):
                        seen.add((ny, nx))
                        stack.append((ny, nx))
            r0, r1 = min(y for y, x in cells), max(y for y, x in cells)
            c0, c1 = min(x for y, x in cells), max(x for y, x in cells)
            border = {(y, x) for y in range(r0, r1 + 1) for x in range(c0, c1 + 1)

            if len(border) >= 8 and border.issubset(cells):

                if ih > 0 and iw > 0:

                    frames.append((color, r0, r1, c0, c1, cells, bitmap))

    matched = set()
    for src in patterned:

        shape = (sr1-sr0+1, sc1-sc0+1)
        for target in frames:

            if target is src or (tr1-tr0+1, tc1-tc0+1) != shape:

            if any(any(row) for row in tbits):

            matched.add(id(target))

                for j, marked in enumerate(row):

    # Empty panels that do not receive a stencil are discarded.

        color, r0, r1, c0, c1, cells, bitmap = frame
        if not any(any(row) for row in bitmap) and id(frame) not in matched:
            for y, x in cells:
                out[y][x] = 0
